newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Fairfax says needs critical mass.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Fairfax says needs critical mass.

text.p: John Fairfax Holdings Ltd chairman Sir Laurence Street said on Wednesday the need for diversification of media ownership was important but a critical mass was necessary to maintain a company's viability.

Street said this was particularly relevant to newspaper publishers, which require significant investment in printing facilities in the present time of rapid technology change, as well as investment in research or new markets.

"Direct access either through proprietorship or through strategic alliances, to the fruits of research and development both in Australia and overseas, is of major importance in assuring the viability of major participants in the newspaper industry in Australia," Street said.
"Economies of scale favour the larger proprietors who can deliver more efficient operations."

Canadian media magnate Conrad Black, who owns 25 percent of Fairfax, has repeatedly said he wanted government permission to increase his stake to at least 35 percent, thus ensuring some protection from his media rivals.

"In conjunction with convergence, globalisation has seen media companies align themselves internationally to take advantage of economies of scale in both production and communications technology," Street added.

Street said that to provide adequate commercial viability of the industry, the regulation of Australia's media industry should be structured so far as possible to minimise the risk of politicisation of media ownership regulation.
Street said these were some of the points the group had made in its submissions to the government's media study.
